Butts (1833-1905); probably among the collection of Butts family drawings and engravings which, according to Geoffrey Keynes, *Bibliotheca Bibliographici* (London: Trianon Press, 1964) 86, "was obtained from the Butts family by the late Joseph Horne and was bought at his sale about 1954 by Mr. E. Guntrip of Maidstone, who sold it to me [Keynes] in 1961; given by Keynes by bequest in 1982 to the Fitzwilliam Museum, which accessioned the work in 1985.

desc.objtitle: Two Views of an Afflicted Child, Object 1 (Essick XLVII)

illustration.illusobjdesc: As the title indicates, there is one figure seen from two different perspectives, facing left in profile and facing forward. The figure is male and a child. His head and neck are the only parts of his body that are pictured. He has short hair and an enlarged face due to swelling on its left side. The view of his face on the left shows what might be a growth or a wound made to alleviate swelling or possibly an incision to expose the lymph nodes. The view of his face on the right shows him facing forward. Both portraits indicate that the boy is suffering from an extreme case of the mumps.
